heroData.title: EOR & PEO Services in Afghanistan
heroData.subtitle: Compliant Hiring and Payroll Management for 2025-2026
heroData.description: Expand your global team to Afghanistan without the need for a local entity. Our EOR services handle localized contracts, payroll withholding, and strict compliance with the latest Labor Law updates and de facto directives.
heroData.bestFor: Enterprises and NGOs seeking rapid market entry without the overhead of entity setup.

steps.title: Contract Drafting & Local Law Review
steps.description: Liaise with local legal counsel to draft employment contracts in Pashto or Dari (or bilingual). Contracts must specify the fixed-term or indefinite nature and include mandatory benefits as per the Afghanistan Labor Law (2007/2024 updates). The contract must be signed in three copies: for the employer, the employee, and the Ministry of Labor.

steps.title: TIN & Social Security Registration
steps.description: Collect employee Identification (NID/Tazkira) and register them with the Ministry of Finance for a Tax Identification Number (TIN). Simultaneously, register the employee with the General Directorate of Labor for social security and pension contributions.

steps.title: Work Permit Application (for Expats)
steps.description: If hiring expatriates, apply for work permits through the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs. This requires valid specialized skills proof, security clearance from the Ministry of Interior, and a local sponsor (the EOR entity).

steps.title: Bank Account Setup Assistance
steps.description: Assist employees in opening local bank accounts for salary disbursement in Afghani (AFN). Note that international transfers can be subject to central bank restrictions, so EOR providers often manage the liquidity logistics.

steps.title: Mandatory Insurance Enrollment
steps.description: Ensure enrollment in statutory work accident insurance. Most EORs also provide supplementary health benefits as part of their package to stay competitive in the local talent market.

steps.title: Initial Payroll Run Setup
steps.description: Set up the payroll cycle in the EOR platform, ensuring all withholdings (Income Tax and Pension) are calculated based on the 2025 tax brackets (0% for income up to 5,000 AFN, scaling to 20%).

items.title: Permanent Establishment (PE) Risk
items.text: Operating via an EOR for extended periods (typically >12 months) without a local entity may eventually trigger Permanent Establishment status for the parent company. Document the temporary nature of the project.

items.title: Termination Notice Periods
items.text: Minimum notice for terminating an indefinite contract is typically 1 month. During probation, this can be as low as 24-48 hours. Always ensure termination grounds are documented in compliance with Article 16 of the Labor Law.

items.title: Currency and Inflation Buffering
items.text: The Afghani (AFN) can experience significant volatility. It is standard practice to peg salaries to USD while converting to AFN at the mid-month exchange rate for compliance.

items.title: Media and Online Activity Monitoring
items.text: Employers should advise employees on local sensitivities regarding social media content. De facto authorities have issued strict directives (2024) regarding online conduct that could impact employment status.

items.title: Annual Paid Leave Entitlements
items.text: Employees are entitled to 20 days of paid annual leave, 20 days of paid sick leave, and 15 days of 'urgent' leave (weddings/funerals) per year.

items.title: Solar Hijri Calendar Integration
items.text: Administrative dates, fiscal cycles, and religious holidays follow the Solar Hijri calendar. Payroll software must be configured to map these correctly to Gregorian dates for reporting.

items.title: Working Week & Rest Days
items.text: Friday is the official weekend. Thursday is often a half-working day in government and many private sectors. Work hours are typically capped at 40 hours per week.

items.title: Religious Observances
items.text: During Ramadan, working hours are reduced by 1-2 hours daily. It is customary to provide small bonuses or food hampers (Eidi) during Eid Al-Fitr and Eid Al-Adha.

items.title: Restrictive Sector Policies
items.text: Recent directives (2023-2024) have imposed restrictions on female employment in certain NGOs and sectors. Employers must coordinate with their EOR to navigate these local constraints.

faqs.question: Can I use an EOR to hire freelancers in Afghanistan?
faqs.answer: Yes, EORs can facilitate the transition from freelance to full employment, providing the worker with statutory benefits and the company with IP protection and compliance.

faqs.question: Are there specific requirements for background checks?
faqs.answer: Yes, EORs typically verify education through local institutions and employment via reference checks. A 'Police Clearance' (No Objection Certificate) from the Ministry of Interior is often required for sensitive roles.

faqs.question: What happens if an employee gets sick?
faqs.answer: The Labor Law provides for 20 days of paid sick leave. For longer-term disability, the employee may be covered under statutory accident insurance managed by the Ministry of Labor.

faqs.question: Is insurance provided by the EOR?
faqs.answer: EORs provide the mandatory state insurance. However, due to the limited capacity of public healthcare, most premium EOR partners include private medical insurance for their staff.

faqs.question: How are intellectual property (IP) rights handled?
faqs.answer: Standard EOR contracts include a clause where the employee assigns all IP rights created during the course of employment to the EOR, who then transfers them to the client via the MSA.

steps.title: Monthly Data Collection
steps.description: Gather attendance, overtime, bonuses, tax-free allowances, and any unpaid leave data (e.g., unpaid urgent leave) by the 18th of the month.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Convert USD salaries to AFN using the approved MoF exchange rate. Calculate gross salary, then subtract the progressive Income Tax and any applicable pension deductions.

steps.title: Compliance Check & Validation
steps.description: Review the payroll results against the latest 2025 tax circulars. Ensure the 'Small Taxpayer' or 'Medium Taxpayer' thresholds are correctly applied to the corporate entity.

steps.title: Approval & Funding
steps.description: The client approves the payroll register. Funds are transferred to the local payroll provider's trust account or directly to Da Afghanistan Bank for tax remittance.

steps.title: Salary Disbursement
steps.description: Salaries are disbursed to employee bank accounts (AIB, Azizi, Kabul Bank, etc.) by the 28th-30th of the month. Digital payslips are issued via the portal.

steps.title: Tax Remittance & Filing
steps.description: The withheld income tax must be filed and remitted to the Ministry of Finance by the 10th of the following month (Article 58 of the Income Tax Law).

items.title: Tax Identification Number (TIN) Mandate
items.text: Salaries cannot be paid to employees without a registered TIN. Processing payments without a TIN results in automatic rejection of the expense for corporate tax purposes.

items.title: Contractor vs Employee Distinction
items.text: Misclassification of employees as contractors is a high-risk area. Local labor inspectors frequently audit payroll records to ensure benefits like annual leave and social security are provided to staff.

items.title: Bonus Tax Treatment
items.text: performance bonuses and 13th-month payments are considered taxable income and must be aggregated with the monthly salary in the period they are paid for tax slab calculations.

items.title: Banking Sector Liquidity
items.text: Due to international sanctions and liquidity limits, withdrawing large amounts of AFN can be difficult. It is advisable to maintain a local balance for payroll to ensure timely payouts.

items.title: AFN Payment Mandate
items.text: All salaries for local employees must be disbursed in Afghan Afghanis (AFN) via bank transfer to comply with DAB regulations, even if the base salary is pegged to USD.

items.title: Social Security Enforcement
items.text: While historically lax in certain private sectors, the current administration is increasing audits of the 11% employer retirement contribution for larger entities.

items.title: Audit of Fixed Allowances
items.text: The Ministry of Finance often treats transport and food allowances as taxable income unless they are backed by specific project-related expense receipts.

items.title: Regional Payroll Variations
items.text: Payroll for employees in different provinces may require separate reporting or coordination with provincial-level Mostofyats (Revenue Offices).

faqs.question: Can I pay employees in USD in Afghanistan?
faqs.answer: While contracts can be denominated in USD, actual bank transfers within Afghanistan are typically required to be in AFN. For expatriates, split-payroll options may be available depending on work permit status.

faqs.question: What are the common payroll deductions?
faqs.answer: The primary deductions are Personal Income Tax (PIT) and Pension contributions. Court-ordered garnishments (e.g., child support) must also be processed if officially notified.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum wage in Afghanistan?
faqs.answer: Yes, there is a minimum wage for the private and NGO sector, which is periodically adjusted. As of 2024, it is generally around 5,000 - 6,000 AFN for unskilled labor.

faqs.question: How do EORs handle payroll for remote teams?
faqs.answer: EORs integrate remote teams into a single local payroll entity, managing the logistics of local banking, tax filings, and compliance from a centralized dashboard.

items.title: Severance Accumulation
items.text: Although not always funded monthly, companies must track severance liability (one month's pay per year of service) to avoid sudden liquidity crises during staff reductions.

items.title: Overtime Calculation
items.text: Overtime is typically calculated at 125% of the hourly rate for extra hours on workdays and 150% for work on holidays/rest days.

items.title: Exchange Rate Volatility
items.text: Official MoF rates for tax calculation may differ from market rates. Always use the MoF published rates for the specific payment month to avoid tax underpayment.

items.title: Gross-to-Net Variance
items.text: Employers must calculate PIT on the gross salary inclusive of fixed allowances (transport, food) unless specific exemptions are granted by the MoF.

items.title: Social Security (Pension)
items.text: For civil service and certain formal sector roles, a 5% employee and 11% employer contribution is standard, though private sector enforcement varies by industry.

items.title: Bonuses and Overtime
items.text: Annual bonuses (13th month) are taxable as regular income in the month they are paid. Ensure the tax slab for that specific month is adjusted accordingly.

steps.title: Determine Gross Base Salary
steps.description: Combine the base pay with all taxable allowances for the month.

steps.title: Subtract Exemptions
steps.description: Identify non-taxable components if any (e.g., approved business expense reimbursements).

steps.title: Apply Marginal Tax Rates
steps.description: Calculate the tax for each band (2%, 10%, 20%) based on the brackets.

steps.title: Duct Fixed Penalties (if applicable)
steps.description: Subtract any disciplinary deductions or loan repayments from the net amount.

steps.title: Final Disbursement
steps.description: Pay the final net amount to the employee's bank account or via cash (with T-Form recognition).

faqs.question: Are transport and food allowances taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, in Afghanistan, the Ministry of Finance generally treats all cash allowances paid with the salary as taxable income.

faqs.question: How often do tax brackets change?
faqs.answer: Tax brackets are established by the Income Tax Law. Changes are rare but occur through legislative decrees or budget adjustments.

faqs.question: Can I use foreign exchange rates for tax filing?
faqs.answer: No, you must use the official exchange rates published by Da Afghanistan Bank (DAB) for the relevant period.

items.title: Mid-Month Starts
items.text: For employees starting mid-month, PIT is usually calculated on the actual earned amount rather than the full nominal monthly salary.

items.title: Rounding Rules
items.text: Ensure that tax calculations are rounded to the nearest Afghani to avoid discrepancies in T-Form filings.

items.title: Software Integration
items.text: Automating these calculations via a localized HRIS helps prevent manual errors in the 20% high-earner tax bracket.

heroData.title: Business Incorporation in Afghanistan
heroData.subtitle: Strategic Entity Setup and Licensing Support
heroData.description: Establish a robust legal foundation in Afghanistan through the Afghanistan Central Business Registry (ACBR). We handle everything from entity selection and name reservation to security clearances and final business licensing.
heroData.bestFor: Industrial investors, Infrastructure firms, and Long-term market participants.

items.title: Private Limited Company (LLC)
items.text: Limited to 50 shareholders. Offers 100% foreign ownership. Requires a registered local office and a designated managing director. This is the preferred vehicle for service providers and traders.

items.title: Foreign Branch Office
items.text: Ideal for multi-national corporations (MNCs) executing specific government or developmental contracts. It simplifies the repatriation of profits but links the parent company to Afghan liabilities.

items.title: Joint Venture (JV)
items.text: Often required for large-scale mining or infrastructure projects. Requires a complex local partnership agreement and specific cabinet-level approvals in some sectors.

items.title: NGO Registration
items.text: NGOs must register via the Ministry of Economy (MoEc) and adhere to strict quarterly reporting requirements and the 'Law on NGOs'.

steps.title: Application & Name Reservation
steps.description: Submit a formal application to the ACBR with three proposed names. The name must be unique and respect cultural norms. Once approved, you receive a 'Name Reservation Certificate'.

steps.title: Document Preparation & Execution
steps.description: Draft the Articles of Association (AoA) and Memorandum of Association (MoA). All documents for foreign shareholders must be notarized and apostilled (if applicable) in the home country.

steps.title: Security & Background Clearance
steps.description: Photos and identification documents of all directors and shareholders are submitted to the ACBR, who سپس coordinates with the Interpol Directorate for background checks.

steps.title: Capital Deposit & Bank fee Payment
steps.description: Pay the registration fees at Da Afghanistan Bank. While there is no strict minimum capital for LLCs in some sectors, a nominal amount (e.g., 50,000 AFN) is often deposited to show intent.

steps.title: Tax ID (TIN) Issuance
steps.description: The ACBR automatically forwards the registered details to the Revenue Department. The company's TIN is usually issued within 3-5 days of registration.

steps.title: License Issuance & Publication
steps.description: The Official Business License is printed. It is mandatory to publish the business registration in a local newspaper and the ACBR official journal.

faqs.question: Can a foreign company be a shareholder?
faqs.answer: Yes, foreign corporations can be 100% owners of an Afghan LLC. The registration will require the parent company's certificates of incorporation and board resolutions.

faqs.question: Is a physical office address mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, a registered physical office within Afghanistan is required. Authorities may perform a 'physical verification' of the premises before issuing certain licenses.

faqs.question: What are the audit requirements for new companies?
faqs.answer: Companies are required to maintain accounting records. For entities above a certain revenue threshold, an annual audit by an approved Afghan auditing firm is mandatory.

faqs.question: How long is the business license valid?
faqs.answer: The initial license is typically valid for three years. It must be renewed with the ACBR to maintain a valid TIN and banking status.

items.title: Industrial Park Incentives
items.text: Companies registered within Kabul or Herat Industrial Parks may be eligible for reduced utility rates and simplified site-verification processes.

items.title: Post-Registration Compliance
items.text: After obtaining the license, a company MUST register with the Ministry of Finance for a TIN and open a local bank account within 30 days.

items.title: Director Residency Requirements
items.text: While directors can be foreign, at least one representative must be locally available or have a valid local power of attorney for ACBR interactions.

heroData.title: Staffing & Talent Acquisition in Afghanistan
heroData.subtitle: Finding Specialized Talent in a Dynamic Market
heroData.description: Access a pool of qualified local and expatriate talent through our specialized recruitment services. We handle everything from executive search to high-volume staffing for NGO and infrastructure projects in Afghanistan.
heroData.bestFor: Organizations needing technical experts, bilingual staff, or project-based workforces.

items.title: Bilingual Professional Scarcity
items.text: Fluency in English alongside Dari and Pashto is a premium skill. Recruitment often targets graduates from international universities (AUAF) or returnees from neighboring countries.

items.title: Passive Candidate Sourcing
items.text: High-quality professionals are often employed by international NGOs. Sourcing requires a network-driven approach rather than reliance on job portals like ACBAR alone.

items.title: Verification and Vetting
items.text: Educational degree verification from the Ministry of Higher Education is mandatory for specialized roles. Security clearances may take several weeks.

items.title: Executive Search in Banking/Finance
items.text: With the evolving regulatory landscape, there is a surge in demand for compliance and risk officers with international certification.

steps.title: Job Profile & KPI Definition
steps.description: Defining roles with clear KPIs that align with both international standards and local operational realities.

steps.title: Multichannel Sourcing
steps.description: Leveraging local platforms (ACBAR, Jobs.af), social media (LinkedIn), and internal talent databases to find matched candidates.

steps.title: Rigorous Skill Assessments
steps.description: Conducting technical assessments, language proficiency tests, and cultural fit interviews tailored to the Afghan business environment.

steps.title: Security & Background Checks
steps.description: Performing comprehensive checks including Tazkira verification, criminal record checks, and employment history audits.

steps.title: Offer Management & Local Contract Prep
steps.description: Negotiating compensation packages (often in USD) and preparing labor-law compliant contracts for signature.

faqs.question: What are the most popular job portals in Afghanistan?
faqs.answer: ACBAR (mainly for NGOs) and Jobs.af are the primary platforms. LinkedIn is gaining traction among higher-level corporate professionals.

faqs.question: How do you verify Afghan educational degrees?
faqs.answer: Verification is done through the Ministry of Higher Education. For international degrees, an 'Equivalency Certificate' is required for certain government-related roles.

faqs.question: Are there recruitment quotas for local staff?
faqs.answer: While not always strictly legislated as a percentage, foreign firms are encouraged to train and prioritize local talent. Work permits for expats are strictly audited to ensure no local replacement is available.

faqs.question: What is the notice period for recruitment service cancellation?
faqs.answer: Standard terms usually require 30 days notice. Retained searches may have specific milestone-based triggers for cancellation fees.

items.title: Solar Hijri Integration
items.text: Recruitment timelines and start dates are often planned around the Solar Hijri calendar, especially the Nowruz (New Year) period.

items.title: Referral-Based Hiring
items.text: The 'Wasta' (connections) system is prevalent. Professional recruitment agencies act as a neutral filter to ensure merit-based hiring while respecting local networks.

items.title: Work Permit Rigor
items.text: Expatriate work permits are issued only if it can be demonstrated that no qualified Afghan national is available for the role, following local labor priority laws.

heroData.title: HRIS Solutions for Afghanistan
heroData.subtitle: Streamlined HR Management & Digital Compliance
heroData.description: Adopt modern HRIS platforms tailored for the Afghan market. Manage employee data, attendance, leave, and local compliance from a single, cloud-based interface with multi-language support.
heroData.bestFor: Scaling businesses and NGOs requiring digital records and automated HR workflows.

items.title: Multi-Calendar Compatibility
items.text: Our HRIS solutions support both the Solar Hijri and Gregorian calendars, ensuring accurate leave and anniversary tracking for local and expat staff.

items.title: Mobile-First Access
items.text: Given high mobile penetration versus desktop, a mobile-responsive HR portal or app is critical for employee self-service in Afghanistan.

items.title: Data Hosting Regulations
items.text: While cloud hosting is common, certain sectors (Banking/NGO) may have specific data sovereignty requirements. Ensure the HRIS partner meets local security standards.

items.title: Biometric Integration
items.text: Many local offices use biometric (fingerprint/face) time and attendance systems. Integrating these with your HRIS eliminates manual data entry errors.

steps.title: HR Audit & Data Cleanup
steps.description: Consolidate existing paper-based or spreadsheet records. Verify current TINs, Tazkira numbers, and contract end dates.

steps.title: Module Configuration
steps.description: Configure leave policies (Urgent, Sick, Annual), tax brackets for 2025, and organization charts based on local reporting lines.

steps.title: Employee Data Import
steps.description: Bulk upload validated data into the secured HRIS environment, ensuring GDPR (or equivalent) data protection protocols.

steps.title: Personnel Training
steps.description: Train HR admins and managers on the platform. Conduct orientation sessions for employees on self-service (payslip access, leave requests).

steps.title: Go-Live & Support
steps.description: Launch the platform and provide hyper-care support for the first two payroll cycles to ensure seamless integration.

items.title: Offline Syncing Protocols
items.text: Due to intermittent internet outages in Kabul and Herat, any HRIS used should have a robust local-storage and auto-sync mechanism.

items.title: Bilingual Database Support
items.text: Ensure that employee names and addresses can be stored in both Dari/Pashto (Unicode) and Latin scripts for compliance and reporting.

items.title: Personal Data Sovereignty
items.text: Under updated 2024 directives, organizations are encouraged to keep a physical mirror of digital HR records within Afghan borders.

faqs.question: Does the system support the local Solar Hijri calendar?
faqs.answer: Yes, our HRIS modules are fully compatible with both Solar Hijri and Gregorian calendars for leave management and attendance tracking.

faqs.question: Can we generate MoF-compliant T-Forms?
faqs.answer: The platform includes custom reporting templates that export payroll data directly into formats acceptable by the Ministry of Finance Revenue Department.

faqs.question: Is employee self-service available via mobile?
faqs.answer: A responsive mobile portal is available, allowing employees to view payslips and request leave from their smartphones, even on low-bandwidth connections.

faqs.question: How is HR data backed up?
faqs.answer: Data is encrypted and backed up daily across multiple secure servers with automated failover systems to ensure 99.9% uptime.

heroData.title: Accounting Services in Afghanistan
heroData.subtitle: IFRS-Compliant Reporting and Financial Management
heroData.description: Maintain financial transparency and regulatory compliance with our expert accounting services in Afghanistan. From bookkeeping to IFRS-compliant financial statements, we handle your local treasury and reporting needs.
heroData.bestFor: Foreign entities requiring high-fidelity financial reporting and local tax audit readiness.

items.title: IFRS Adoption
items.text: Afghanistan has adopted International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). All foreign-invested companies are expected to prepare their annual reports according to these standards.

items.title: MoF Audit Readiness
items.text: The Ministry of Finance Revenue Department often conducts 'Site Audits'. Keeping a physical 'Asset Register' and sequential voucher filing is mandatory.

items.title: Expense Deductibility
items.text: Expenses must be documented with MoF-approved invoices. Many 'cash only' local purchases without formal receipts may be disallowed during corporate tax assessment.

items.title: Statutory Ledger Requirements
items.text: maintenance of a General Ledger, Purchase Journal, and Sales Journal in a serialized format (often requiring official stamps) is a traditional but critical requirement.

steps.title: Bank Reconciliation
steps.description: Reconcile local AFN accounts and international USD accounts, ensuring all transaction fees and exchange rate variances are recorded.

steps.title: Accruals & Prepayments
steps.description: Record monthly accruals for rent, utilities, and employee bonuses to ensure accurate profit/loss reporting.

steps.title: WHT Reconciliation
steps.description: Ensure the Withholding Tax (WHT) on vendor payments and payroll matches the monthly tax returns submitted to the STO/MTO.

steps.title: Financial Statement Prep
steps.description: Draft the Income Statement, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow statement for management review.

steps.title: Local Tax Provisioning
steps.description: Calculate estimated Corporate Income Tax (20%) and ensure adequate funds are reserved.

items.title: Petty Cash Management
items.text: Maintain a strict petty cash log with serialized vouchers. Local 'Sarai' market purchases must be documented with a vendor Tazkira copy whenever possible.

items.title: Dual-Currency Ledgers
items.text: Most international firms maintain ledgers in both AFN (for statutory filing) and USD (for management reporting). Ensure the MoF month-end rate is used for conversions.

items.title: Vendor Withholding Tax
items.text: Ensure you withhold the correct percentage (2% or 7%) on all local vendor payments to avoid being held liable for their tax during your audit.

faqs.question: Can we use QuickBooks or Xero for Afghan accounting?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they must be configured with a custom Afghan Chart of Accounts that maps to the Ministry of Finance's reporting requirements.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for undocumented expenses?
faqs.answer: The MoF will simply disallow the expense, increasing your taxable profit and resulting in a 20% CIT hit on those amounts.

faqs.question: Are digital records sufficient for a tax audit?
faqs.answer: No, the Revenue Department still requires physical 'Hard Copies' of all vouchers and bank statements, sequentially filed and easily accessible.

faqs.question: How do we handle exchange rate gains/losses?
faqs.answer: Realized gains/losses must be recorded in the monthly P&L. Unrealized gains/losses are typically adjusted at year-end per IFRS standards.

items.title: CPA Afghanistan Oversight
items.text: All statutory audits must be performed by firms registered with the Certified Public Accountants (CPA) office under the Ministry of Finance.

items.title: Quarterly Performance Tracking
items.text: While CIT is annual, the Revenue Department tracks 'Interim Compliance' through quarterly BRT filings. An audit trail for these quarterly payments is essential for year-end clearance.

items.title: Anti-Money Laundering (AML)
items.text: DAB (Central Bank) regulations on AML/CFT (Counter-Financing of Terrorism) have intensified for 2025. Businesses must maintain strict KYC records for all significant transactions.

items.title: NGO-Specific Requirements
items.text: NGOs must submit semi-annual project reports to the Ministry of Economy. These reports are often audited before the next tranche of project approval.

steps.title: Audit Planning & Risk Assessment
steps.description: Reviewing the organization's structure, internal controls, and identifying high-risk areas in local procurement and payroll.

steps.title: Fieldwork & Evidence Gathering
steps.description: Conducting on-site visits, verifying physical assets, and sampling financial vouchers for compliance with IFRS and local MoF directives.

steps.title: Draft Report & Management Letter
steps.description: Sharing preliminary findings with management, highlighting internal control weaknesses and tax exposures.

steps.title: Final Opinion Issuance
steps.description: Issuing the Independent Auditor's Report (Qualified, Unqualified, or Disclaimer) as per ISAs.

steps.title: MoF Submission & Support
steps.description: Assisting management in presenting the audited statements to the Revenue Department for final tax assessment.

items.title: Conflict of Interest
items.text: The Ministry of Finance prohibits the same firm from providing both statutory audit and accounting/tax filing services for the same entity in the same fiscal year.

items.title: Transparency Portals
items.text: Recent 2024 directives encourage firms to upload audited financials to a centralized MoF portal for 'E-Governance' transparency initiatives.

items.title: Internal Controls (ERM)
items.text: Effective Enterprise Risk Management in Afghanistan should prioritize physical security, cash transport protocols, and dual-authorization for all local payments.

faqs.question: Are international accounting firms available in Kabul?
faqs.answer: While some 'Big 4' firms have local affiliations, many statutory audits are performed by high-tier local firms registered with CPA Afghanistan that follow international ISAs.

faqs.question: What happens if we receive a 'Qualified' audit opinion?
faqs.answer: The Revenue Department may flag the 'Qualifications' for higher scrutiny during tax assessment, potentially leading to disallowed expenses or higher CIT liability.

faqs.question: How long should we keep compliance records?
faqs.answer: Under Afghan Law, financial and compliance records must be preserved for at least 10 years, preferably in both physical and secure digital formats.

faqs.question: Is internal audit mandatory?
faqs.answer: For private firms, it is optional but highly recommended. For NGOs and public agencies, it is often a donor-mandated or statutory requirement.

items.title: Standard Corporate Rate
items.text: Legal entities in Afghanistan are subject to a flat 20% Corporate Income Tax (CIT) on their net taxable income.

items.title: Business Receipts Tax (BRT)
items.text: BRT is a gross revenue tax (typically 4% for services and high-level entities) that must be filed quarterly. It is paid regardless of whether the company is profitable.

items.title: Dividend Withholding (Art 46)
items.text: Dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents are subject to a 20% withholding tax at source.

items.title: Advance Tax on Imports
items.text: Registered businesses pay a 2% advance income tax on total value (including customs) of imported goods, which is later creditable against annual CIT.

steps.title: Preparation of Trial Balance
steps.description: Ensure all entries for the fiscal year (ending Dec 31 or per your approved cycle) are finalized.

steps.title: Tax Reconciliation & Adjusted Profit
steps.description: Add back non-deductible expenses (e.g., entertainment, undocumented cash payments) to the accounting profit.

steps.title: Filing of Income Tax Return
steps.description: Submit the annual tax return to the relevant office (STO/MTO/LTO) within 3 months of the fiscal year-end (usually by March 31).

steps.title: Assessment & Clearance
steps.description: Wait for the Revenue Department assessment. Upon agreement and payment, obtain a 'Tax Clearance Certificate' mandatory for license renewal.

items.title: Loss Carry Forward
items.text: Net operating losses can be carried forward for up to five subsequent years, providing a shield against future profits.

items.title: Monthly PIT Focus
items.text: Revenue inspectors prioritize Payroll Income Tax (PIT) audits. Ensure every employee has an individual TIN linked to their payroll record.

items.title: Zero-Return Penalty
items.text: Even if your company has no revenue, you MUST file a 'nil' BRT return quarterly. Failure to do so incurs an automatic late fee.

faqs.question: Is there a VAT system in Afghanistan?
faqs.answer: A Value Added Tax (VAT) Law was introduced but its implementation has faced several delays and suspensions. BRT currently remains the primary consumption-based tax.

faqs.question: Are there Double Taxation Treaties (DTT)?
faqs.answer: Afghanistan has limited DTTs. Most foreign firms rely on unilateral tax credits in their home countries for Afghan taxes paid.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late BRT filing?
faqs.answer: Late filing of BRT returns results in a fixed fine (approx 500 AFN per day) plus 0.1% daily interest on the unpaid tax amount.

faqs.question: Do NGOs pay Corporate Income Tax?
faqs.answer: Organizations registered as NPOs/NGOs are generally exempt from CIT on their charitable activities but must still withhold PIT on salaries and WHT on vendor payments.

heroData.title: M&A & Contractual Frameworks for Afghanistan
heroData.subtitle: Protecting Interests in a High-Growth Frontier
heroData.description: Establish clear, enforceable Master Service Agreements and manage M&A legal frameworks that bridge international standards with local reality. We help structure templates for vendor management and strategic transactions.
heroData.bestFor: International agencies, project implementers, and firms seeking stable contractual and strategic foundations.

items.title: Dispute Resolution Strategy
items.text: While local courts are an option, many international firms specify arbitration in neutral jurisdictions like Dubai (DIAC) or Singapore (SIAC). Enforceability of foreign awards is a complex but necessary consideration.

items.title: Force Majeure Clausing
items.text: Given the operational environment, MSAs must include robust Force Majeure clauses that specifically cover political shifts, internet shutdowns, and security lockdowns.

items.title: Bilingual Contracts
items.text: Contracts should ideally be in English and either Dari or Pashto. In case of local court disputes, the local language version often takes precedence.

items.title: Currency Hedge Clauses
items.text: With the AFN/USD volatility, MSAs should define strict exchange rates for invoicing or allow for monthly adjustments based on DAB (Central Bank) mid-market rates.

steps.title: Requirement Scoping
steps.description: Clearly define the Statement of Work (SOW), service levels (SLAs), and specific deliverables tailored to the Afghan context.

steps.title: Legal Template Selection
steps.description: Select the appropriate MSA template (Global Master vs. Local Specific) and adapt clauses for local labor and tax laws.

steps.title: Negotiated Review
steps.description: Iterate on terms with local stakeholders and legal counsel to ensure risk parity and compliance with Ministry of Economy guidelines.

steps.title: Execution & Attestation
steps.description: Obtain formal signatures. For high-value contracts, consider attestation by the Chamber of Commerce or ACBR.

steps.title: Compliance Monitoring
steps.description: Establish a regular review cycle to assess vendor performance, insurance validity, and tax clearance renewals.

items.title: Governing Law Choices
items.text: While many stick to 'English Law', recent trends suggest 'DIFC Law' (Dubai) as a preferred middle ground for Middle Eastern and Central Asian projects.

items.title: Indemnity Caps
items.text: Aggressive indemnity clauses are hard to enforce locally. Focus on performance bonds or escrow mechanisms for critical projects.

items.title: Project Suspension Rights
items.text: Always include a clear suspension clause allowing the provider to stop services without breach in case of security deterioration.

faqs.question: Are electronic signatures legally recognized in Afghanistan?
faqs.answer: The Law on Electronic Transactions recognizes digital signatures, but many government departments still insist on 'Wet Signatures' and official stamps (Chapa) for formal documents.

faqs.question: What is the limitation of liability standard?
faqs.answer: Standard commercial practice in Afghanistan often limits liability to the total value of fees paid under the specific SOW/Order Form, excluding cases of gross negligence.

faqs.question: Do I need to notarize all commercial contracts?
faqs.answer: While not always legally required for B2B services, notarization or registration with the ACBR can provide additional evidence of authenticity in case of local litigation.

faqs.question: How do we handle IP rights in MSAs?
faqs.answer: Software and creative projects should explicitly state 'Work for Hire' terms. Afghanistan has basic IP laws, but protective contractual language is your primary defense.

heroData.title: Enterprise Software & Digital Tools
heroData.subtitle: Modernizing Operations with Tailored SaaS
heroData.description: Deploy scalable software solutions that work in the Afghan context. From Cloud ERP to mobile data collection tools, we help you overcome connectivity challenges and manage growth digitally.
heroData.bestFor: Growing businesses needing automated inventory, CRM, or data management systems.

items.title: Cloud Adoption vs. Local Hosting
items.text: Cloud ERP market is growing (expected 12% CAGR). However, for mission-critical apps, hybrid models with local caching are preferred to mitigate internet instability.

items.title: Inventory & Supply Chain Integration
items.text: Real-time tracking of imports and warehouse movement is a high-demand feature for the logistics and wholesale sectors in Kabul and Herat.

items.title: Payment Gateway Limitations
items.text: Direct integration with international payment gateways (Stripe/PayPal) is currently restricted. Local software often uses bank-transfer integrations or manual verification workflows.

items.title: Open Source Customization
items.text: Many Afghan firms leverage Odoo or ERPNext due to their open-source nature, allowing for deep customization of local tax and payroll modules.

steps.title: System Needs Analysis
steps.description: Mapping existing manual workflows and identifying performance bottlenecks in the current setup.

steps.title: Software Selection & Localization
steps.description: Selecting the right SaaS/ERP and configuring Dari/Pashto interfaces and Solar Hijri calendar support.

steps.title: Offline-First Sync Strategy
steps.description: Ensuring the software can function during internet outages and sync data when connectivity is restored.

steps.title: User Acceptance Testing (UAT)
steps.description: Iterative testing with local staff to ensure the UI is intuitive and meets operational requirements.

steps.title: Data Migration & Go-Live
steps.description: Cleansing old data and migrating it to the new environment under strict security protocols.

items.title: Mobile UX Optimization
items.text: Software used in field operations must be optimized for low-end Android devices, as these are the standard for data entry staff.

items.title: Cybersecurity Resilience
items.text: Use multi-factor authentication (MFA) and encrypted local storage. Given the risk profile, routine automated off-site backups (to regional data centers) are essential.

items.title: Vendor Lock-in Risks
items.text: Prioritize software with easy data export features (CSV/API) to ensure business continuity if a vendor's local presence is disrupted.

faqs.question: Can we host our data on local Afghan servers?
faqs.answer: Yes, several high-tier local ISPs offer server co-location and VPS services in Kabul that meet standard security requirements while reducing latency.

faqs.question: Does the software support the 1399-1400+ Solar Hijri years?
faqs.answer: All our recommended solutions are tested for the unique Afghan leap-year logic and date formatting used in government reporting.

faqs.question: How is technical support provided?
faqs.answer: We offer a blend of remote 24/7 support and on-site emergency technicians in Kabul, Herat, and Mazar-i-Sharif.

faqs.question: Can we integrate biometric hardware with the software?
faqs.answer: Our software solutions offer standard APIs for integration with ZKTeco and other biometric devices commonly used in the region.

heroData.title: Marketing & Strategic Liaison in Afghanistan
heroData.subtitle: Navigating Communication in a Regulated Market
heroData.description: Strategic marketing and advertising services tailored for the Afghan market. We help brands manage community relations, physical media, and compliant online presence amidst changing regulations.
heroData.bestFor: FMCG brands, local startups, and organizations needing public relations and community trust-building.

items.title: Digital Platform Restrictions
items.text: As of Oct 2025, several major social media platforms face intentional technical restrictions. Marketing spends are shifting to Telegram, WhatsApp Business, and local news portals.

items.title: Outdoor Media Authority
items.text: All billboards and physical signage require specific permits from the Kabul Municipality and the Ministry of Information and Culture. Content must strictly adhere to local values.

items.title: Radio Ads for Mass Reach
items.text: In rural provinces, radio remains the most effective medium for mass-market messaging, often bypassing digital literacy barriers.

items.title: B2B Events and Expos
items.text: Industry-specific expos in Kabul and Mazar-e-Sharif are the core hubs for high-level business networking and B2B marketing.

faqs.question: Is influencer marketing popular in Afghanistan?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it is moving from 'Lifestyle' to 'Information' niches. Tech and business influencers on YouTube and TikTok still have significant reach despite restrictions.

faqs.question: What are the restrictions on visual content?
faqs.answer: Images of people (especially women) in advertisements are subject to strict decency and doctrinal guidelines. Many brands now use abstract graphics, calligraphy, or product-focused visuals.

faqs.question: How is the ROI on digital ads measured locally?
faqs.answer: Since direct e-commerce tracking is difficult, ROI is typically measured through 'Call-to-Action' leads via WhatsApp or store-visit footfall increases.

steps.title: Strategic Consultation
steps.description: Reviewing business objectives and target demographics (e.g., Kabul urban youth vs. agricultural traders). Preparing a compliant messaging strategy.

steps.title: Regulatory Clearance
steps.description: Submitting ad creatives to the Ministry of Information and Culture if required, and securing municipal permits for outdoor placements.

steps.title: Media Placement & Execution
steps.description: Coordinating with local radio stations, TV channels, or social media networks for content delivery and live monitoring.

items.title: Language Sensitivity
items.text: Ad campaigns should ideally be bilingual (Dari and Pashto) to ensure national reach and avoid regional favoritism.

items.title: Public Trust Importance
items.text: Word-of-mouth and community liaison officers are often more influential than high-budget digital ads in building long-term brand trust.

items.title: Event Sponsorship
items.text: Sponsoring local sports events (like Buzkashi or Cricket) is a high-impact way to gain brand visibility and communal goodwill.
